RagShortTexts: Uglich draws on Volga traffic and fields; landings require local knowledge.
Unloading, boat repairs and ferries share crews whose plans change with water levels.

Variants.Content: Uglich's bend offers river travelers a recognizable landmark among settlements sustained by fields, transport and exchange. Boats need landings, unloading and repair space shared under local authority. Changing Volga levels and ice can make a familiar berth unusable, so travelers need boatmen's advice as well as a town's name.

Uglich households combine ferrying and grain carriage with fields and animals. A boat owner asks about weight, destination and payment for the return, since a passenger may displace his own delivery. Bad water or wind can justify postponement; a lost day's trade costs less than a lost boat.
